# Project records

Records live in the user's repo and are versioned with the code. Work log lives in issues and PRs, not in a separate log file. Repo know-how (commands, conventions) belongs in the repo's `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `docs/<topic>/discussion.md` | The goal record, below |
| `docs/<topic>/spec.md` | The spec |
| `docs/<topic>/reviews/review-<round>.md` | Review reports; audits beside them as `review-<round>.audit.md` |
| `GLOSSARY.md` | Domain terms |
| `docs/adr/NNNN-<title>.md` | Decisions that are hard to reverse, surprising, or a real trade-off |

`<topic>` is a short lowercase slug of the goal.

## discussion.md

Exactly these second-level headings, in this order. A script checks them.

```markdown
# <topic> - discussion

## Original words

> the user's words, verbatim; later additions appended below, each with its date

## Finish line

- C1 <result> evidence: <what outside the agent proves it: a command and its expected output, a file position, a measured number>
- C2 <result>
  Evidence: <same>

## Authorizations

> only what the user said, quoted, with the date. Never write one yourself.

## Decisions

- YYYY-MM-DD user|agent: <decision> (<reason>)

## Open questions

- <what is unresolved, and the next step>
```

Rules:

- Each finish-line item starts `- C<n> ` and carries `evidence:` (any case) on the line or an `Evidence:` line under it.
- Write results, not methods. Keep to the user's words; a bigger version or better route goes to Decisions as an option.
- A line only the user can judge says `evidence: user judges`.
- Before accepting a line, ask: what would the best person in this field do beyond this? Which rawest data does it start from? Which method and tools? What outside evidence settles it? Fold the first three answers into the line or the verify commands.
- Record the verify commands and the CI status (file, commands it runs) under Decisions.

## GLOSSARY.md

One entry per term the work coins or fixes the meaning of: `**Term**: one-sentence definition. Avoid: <synonyms not to use>`. Use the terms in tickets and code names. Update it when a decision changes a meaning.

## ADR

Write one only when a decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and a real trade-off. Format: title, `Status: accepted`, Context, Decision, Consequences, each one to three sentences. Link it from the Decisions line.
# Tickets

A ticket is one verifiable behavior, written so an implementer with no other context can do it and a reviewer can check it.

## Where

- Repo has a GitHub remote and `gh` is logged in: one GitHub issue per ticket.
- Otherwise (local fallback): one file per ticket at `docs/<topic>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, with a `Status:` line near the top (`open`, `claimed`, `done`) and comments appended under `## Comments`. Resolving a ticket sets `Status: done` and appends the commit.

## Marker

Every issue (or file) and every PR body contains `<!-- agent-flow:<topic>#<NN> -->` with `<NN>` the two-digit ticket number. Before creating one, search for the marker and reuse a match. Search: `gh issue list --state all --search '"agent-flow:<topic>#<NN>" in:body'` and `gh pr list --state all --search '"agent-flow:<topic>#<NN>" in:body'`; in the local fallback, grep `docs/<topic>/issues/`.

## Required fields

```markdown
**What to build:** the behavior, end to end, in a few sentences.

**Blocked by:** #<n>, or "none".

**Scope:** files or modules the work may touch.

**Out of scope:** what the implementer must not do.

- [ ] acceptance criterion, observable

**Verify:**
- `<command run as written>` -> <result that means PASS>

<!-- agent-flow:<topic>#<NN> -->
```

- Title: imperative, names the behavior.
- Verify: every command runs as written from the repo root and says what PASS looks like. A check that needs a person or a browser says so and says how.
- A ticket that changes a user interface lists how it handles waiting, empty results, failure, repeated actions, keyboard operation, and where focus lands after re-render.
- Tickets that change CI or tests are ordinary tickets; the agent merges them.
- A ticket with no code (docs, config) needs no test-first step.

## Dispatch message to the implementer

Only: ticket location (issue number or file path), `docs/<topic>/discussion.md` path, working directory, integration branch, verify commands. Always include: "Any judgment or 'I guess' you make yourself, however small, counts as a guess, so the status cannot be DONE."

Report back: status (`DONE`, `GUESSED`, `BLOCKED`), PR URL, commit, each Verify command with its result, the guess list, what was not verified.

Handling a report: judge each guess. Correct guesses go into the ticket as a comment; wrong ones: revert those commits, fix the ticket, re-dispatch. `GUESSED` with all guesses correct counts as `DONE`. `BLOCKED` goes back to the clarity gate. A second `BLOCKED`, or a second revert, on one ticket means stuck.

Order: intake, finish line, research and CI, spec and tickets, clarity gate, dispatch, check, merge, report. Do the work yourself where thinking is needed (breaking down, deciding); give execution to implementer subagents and judgment of the result to a reviewer in a separate context. Independent work may run in parallel subagents.

Commit after each step. Commit and push to working branches without asking. Every change reaches the default branch through a PR.

## 1. Intake

| The user gives | You do | Start when |
|---|---|---|
| **Goal**: a result they want | Write it as a finish line | Written |
| **Direction**: end point undecided | Research, propose 2-3 candidate finish lines, each with cost and a recommendation | The user picks one |
| **Seed**: a loose idea | Research feasibility and similar work; ask only what cannot be found (preferences, resources, limits), at most 5 questions per round, each with a suggested answer; then propose 2-3 concepts with finish lines | The user picks one |

When unsure which, treat it as the more mature kind and say how you judged. Put the user's words in `discussion.md` verbatim (format: [records.md](records.md)).

## 2. Finish line

- Results, not methods. The user's words bound the scope. First ask what the user wants to happen after this is done; a larger version or better route goes into Decisions as an option, and you work to the original words meanwhile.
- Every line has external evidence: a test, a command, a measured number, a reproduction from raw data. If only the user can judge it, write `evidence: user judges`.
- Apply the four questions from [records.md](records.md).

## 3. Research and CI first

Research order: official docs, source code, web search, then a trial run. Record sources. If the network or a site is blocked, switch source; if a site is truly needed, tell the user which and why.

Find the repo's verify commands in its `package.json`, CI config, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. Record them. If PRs have no CI running them, adding CI is ticket 01: CI runs only the verify commands, with no deploy and no secrets. If the default branch has no rule requiring a PR and green CI, set it when the plan allows (`gh api` branch protection); if not allowed, say so in Decisions, and `merge_gate.py` is the guard.

Missing infrastructure that blocks evidence (raw data or logs, version and commit mapping, a reproducible environment) becomes early tickets. Using secrets, money or the user's own data in this step triggers the `WARNING:` tier; a need for accounts you do not have, or for browser use, goes to the user.

## 4. Spec and tickets

Write `docs/<topic>/spec.md`, then tickets by [tickets.md](tickets.md). You decide the breakdown and record why in Decisions; do not quiz the user. Each ticket is one verifiable behavior.

## 5. Clarity gate

Anything needing a trade-off, a design choice or a question to the user is settled by you before dispatch, then written into the ticket.

Once per batch, before first dispatch, start a fresh subagent. Give it only the ticket locations. Ask: what would you build for each ticket, and where must you guess? Add only guesses that would change a Verify result or an interface between tickets; the rest the implementer reports as `GUESSED`.

Then run every ticket's Verify commands on the unimplemented tree. Those meant to fail must fail for the stated reason. Each command must be correct and finish by itself, leaving no server or process running.

## 6. Dispatch

One subagent per ticket (`subagent_type: agent-flow:implementer`), one worktree each: `git worktree add ../<repo>-<NN> -b <topic>/<NN> <integration branch>`. Message and report format: [tickets.md](tickets.md). After a subagent ends, check for leftover processes (`pgrep -fl`, `lsof` to confirm the owner before killing) and remove its worktree when its PR is merged.

Follow-ups that belong to the finish line become new tickets; anything beyond it goes into Decisions as a question.

Stuck means: the same problem, including a FAIL on the same finish-line item, survives three different approaches; or the next step needs something only the user can give. Save the work, tell the user with options and a recommendation, and continue unblocked work.

## 7. Check and merge

Deterministic checks come first: the verify commands, each finish-line item's evidence, and CI on the PR. Fix failures before any reviewer runs. Then review and audit per [review.md](review.md) and [audit.md](audit.md), and merge only through `merge_gate.py`.

Merge with a merge commit (`gh pr merge <n> --merge`), never squash, so `git revert -m 1 <sha>` undoes it. Record each merge and its evidence in the final report. Deploy and publish are outside the flow: ask first.

## 8. Report

Close with: finish line items, each with its evidence and result; which checks failed or did not run; what was merged; guesses taken and fallbacks used; number of questions to the user and the reason for each. Format: [grounded-answer.md](grounded-answer.md).
# Review

Run the deterministic gate first, then one independent review. Anything a command can verify never goes to an LLM.

## 1. Deterministic gate

Run the project's verify commands and every finish-line item's verify command. CI on the PR runs them again. On failure, return to implementation; no reviewer is started.

## 2. One review

Start a `reviewer` that took no part in the implementation. Give it the original words, the finish line, the project's test and CI commands, the location of the work, the diff range, and an **evidence pack**:

- the diff itself;
- the commands the gate ran, with an output summary;
- for each finish-line item, file excerpts as `path:line` plus the original text.

The reviewer works from the pack. It does not re-run a gate command whose output is in the pack; it writes that command into the report so the audit re-runs it in a sandbox. Write the dispatch message to a file and start the reviewer with `review.py <prompt-file> --cwd <repo>`. Aim for at most 25k tokens per review; trim the pack when it runs over.

The reviewer:

- judges every finish-line item PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN, re-running the external evidence itself. The implementer's report is never evidence.
- reviews what the gate cannot: intent against the spec, shortcuts around the problem (sleep or timeout, swallowed errors, tests changed to pass), security and data risk. Only a problem that changes behavior, rules or acceptance results is a FAIL. Wording, comments and stale phrasing go under `## Findings outside the criteria`, which never blocks a merge.

## 3. Report

Save to `docs/<topic>/reviews/review-<round>.md`, in this format:

```
# Review: <topic> round <n>

Reviewer model: <model>
Reviewed commit: <full sha>
Base: <full sha>            (optional)

### C1 — PASS
Criterion: <text>
Command: `<command run from the repo root>`
Output contains: `<text>`

### C2 — PASS
Criterion: <text>
Position: `<repo-relative path>:<line>`
Contains: `<text>`

### C3 — FAIL
Criterion: <text>
Reproduce: `<command>`
Actual contains: `<text>`
Expected: <text>

### C4 — UNKNOWN
Criterion: <text>
Missing: <what would be needed>

## Rebuttal
### C3
Reason: <text>
Command: `<command>`
Output contains: `<text>`
```

- Item headings are exactly `### <ID> — PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN` (em dash). Other headings must not contain PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN or Rebuttal.
- Every evidence source line (`Command`, `Reproduce`, `Position`) is followed by one expectation line (`Output contains`, `Actual contains`, `Contains`). Expectations are at least 2 characters, except `[exit N]`, which matches the exit-code line `audit.py` appends to command output. To check an exit code, write ``Output contains: `[exit 0]` ``.
- An item may carry several evidence pairs. Pick an expectation that appears only on success: write `OK`, not `Ran 33 tests`, which a failing run prints too.
- A code problem is an item too: each behavior-changing problem is one FAIL whose `Criterion` names the standard or spec line it breaks. With no problems, a PASS item states the range checked, with evidence.

### Which commands the audit runs how

- `Position` is read directly from the file.
- A read-only command (on the argv allowlist in `audit.py`) runs without a shell.
- Any other command is a project command: it runs only inside the sandbox (no network, no `claude`, writes confined to a temporary worktree). If the evidence needs the network or `claude`, give a `Position` instead, or mark the item UNKNOWN and say what is missing.

## 4. After the report

Audit every report (see `audit.md`). The main session never edits the audit.

- **FAIL**: if the evidence holds, fix, re-run the gate, and start a new reviewer for the next round. If it does not hold, write a `## Rebuttal` in the same report with evidence, then audit again.
- **Next round reviews**: items that were FAIL, items the audit found unsound or under-evidenced, and items touching files this fix changed. Other audited PASS items are not re-reviewed.
- **Review passes** when the latest round has no FAIL and every item has an audited PASS in some round (or an UNKNOWN left for the user to judge).
- **At most two rounds.** If round 2 still has a FAIL, or an item went from PASS to FAIL, stop and list the remaining problems for the user. Do not run a third round.
- **UNKNOWN**: if the missing tool, environment or permission can be supplied, supply it and review again. Otherwise list the item as "done but unverified" and say what is missing.
- Merge only after `scripts/merge_gate.py <pr-number>` exits 0; it prints why when blocked.
# Audit

The audit checks that a review report stands: it re-runs the report's evidence. Run it on every report, every round:

```sh
python3 <plugin>/scripts/audit.py docs/<topic>/reviews/review-<round>.md --repo <repo>
```

It writes `review-<round>.audit.md` next to the report. Exit 0 passed, 1 failed, 3 partly unverified, 2 usage or setup error. The audit makes no `claude` call.

## Three states

- **passed**: every piece of evidence re-ran and its expectation appeared.
- **failed**: evidence is missing or malformed (a PASS without evidence, a FAIL without a reproduce command, an UNKNOWN without `Missing`, a Rebuttal without evidence), or an expectation did not appear. Fix what the audit points at, then save a new review as the next round. A finished report is never edited; add a Rebuttal instead.
- **partly unverified**: project commands could not run because no sandbox (macOS Seatbelt, Linux bwrap) is available. This blocks the merge. The audit lists the commands under `## Run these yourself`; give them to the user to run. The user may opt in, for that one run, to running them without a sandbox with `--unsandboxed`. The audit then records `WARNING: project commands ran without a sandbox`. Never pass `--unsandboxed` without that opt-in.

The result is the last line of the `.audit.md`: `Result: passed`, `Result: failed` or `Result: partly unverified`.

## Rules come from the installed plugin

The rules and `audit.py` are the ones in the installed plugin version, not the working tree. `.audit.md` records `Plugin version: <version>`. Never edit `audit.py`, the canaries or a `.audit.md` to make a report pass. If you disagree with an audit, give the report, the audit and your reason to the user; the main session cannot overturn it.

Spot-check, done by the user outside the session: clone the repo at that version's tag and re-run the audit.

```sh
git clone --branch v<version> <plugin repo url> <empty dir>
python3 <empty dir>/plugins/agent-flow/scripts/audit.py <report> --repo <repo>
```

The result must match the recorded `.audit.md`.

Canaries (trap reports the auditor must reject) are run by the maintainer before a release, never on a user's machine. Their stamp ships in the plugin; `audit.py` refuses to run when it is for another version.

## Merge gate

Merge only when `merge_gate.py <pr-number>` exits 0:

- CI is green;
- the highest-round `.audit.md` among the PR's changed files ends `Result: passed`;
- `.agent-flow/STOP` is absent and `.agent-flow/config` has no `merge: never`.

A blocked gate prints one `BLOCKED:` reason per line; fix the reason, do not bypass the gate.
